4. The parties are disputing over owner-ship of land originally belonging to tenants Lai Miah, Baicha Miah, Moni Miah, and Ledu Miah, each holding an equal 4 annas share in C.S. Khatian No. 242 of Mouza Senpara Parbata. After the deaths of the unmarried Baicha and Moni Miah, Lai and Ledu Miah each owned an 8 annas share. Leclu Miah's share passed to his wife Alekun Nessa and daughter Belayetun Nessa, while Lal Miah's share went to his daughters Taherun and Shaherun Nessa. Alekun and Belayetun Nessa sold part of their share to Taherun Nessa, who constructed a house and planted trees on the land. After Shaherun Nessa's death, her heirs inherited her share, and portions were sold to the plaintiffs, who developed the land, paid taxes, and were assigned plots in Partition Suit No. 311 of 1989. 

 12. The lower Appellate court affirmed the decree of the trial court on agreeing with all the positive findings thereof including that of the cardinal point of possession of the plaintiffs on evidence both oral and documentary. The plain-tiffs submitted certified copies of the namjari khatian in their names, along with the D.C.R., rent receipts, city corporation holding tax payment receipts, and the plan obtained from RAJUK for building construction on the disputed property. Additionally, in Partition Case No. 311/89, they received separate sahams (plots) for 35 decimals of land in Dag No. 1347 and 5 decimals of land in Dag No. 1348, and a final decree has been passed regarding the said property. Since the plaintiffs have obtained a final .decree regarding the disputed property through the court, and it has been deter-mined through a court survey that the plaintiffs have ownership and exclusive possession of the disputed property we count the concurrent findings of both the courts below on that score as reliable and tenable.
